newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Korean envoys in new round of talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Korean envoys in new round of talks.

text.p: Diplomats from the United States, South Korea and North Korea began a new round of talks on Monday toward negotiating a peace treaty to end the 1950-53 Korean War, a U.S. State Department official said.
He said senior envoys from the three countries appeared to be in a relaxed mood, shaking hands and exchanging pleasantries before the one-day meeting started in a New York hotel.

North Korean and South Korean delegation leaders told each other they hoped for good results from the meeting, a follow-up to one held in March to discuss a proposal by Washington and Seoul for four-nation peace talks that would eventually also involve China.
The proposed four-party negotiations would aim to replace the armistice of 1953 with a formal peace treaty. The two Koreas are technically still at war.

According to the U.S. official who briefed reporters, North Korean delegation leader Vice Foreign Minister Kim Gye Gwan said: "Last time we were concerned that there might be a premature baby, but this time we're not concerned about a premature baby."
The South Korean delegation is led by Deputy Foreign Minister Song Yong Shik.
Communist North Korea, threatened by famine, agreed in principle in April to join the peace talks but linked its participation to food aid and an end to U.S. trade sanctions.
Political analysts say Pyongyang has agreed to join the four-way talks in a policy shift designed to hold the reclusive state together.
They say that with famine and a ruined economy, the Stalinist government needs to repair its relationship with Western countries who could provide much-needed assistance.
In the relaxed exchanges before Monday's meeting began, U.S. delegation leader Charles Kartman joked with his counterparts, the U.S. official said.

He quoted Kartman as saying, "let me tell you about American boxing...", a reference to Saturday's World Boxing Association heavyweight title fight in which challenger Mike Tyson was disqualified for biting both ears of champion Evander Holyfield.
